//: The frozen release constants (distribution spec §7.6, EDP-30). These are the values an installed VibeField is KNOWN BY: bundle id, publisher, tray slot, update origin. Changing one after a public release is a migration — signatures, update feeds, taskbar pinning and notification routing all key off them — never a cosmetic edit. Two laws are enforced by scripts/check-release-identity.mjs: (1) nothing here may be inferred from a local path, username or hostname (EDP-30) — a value that differs per developer machine is not an identity; (2) a `frozen` field cannot change without bumping identityRevision in the same commit, so an identity edit is always a reviewable event rather than a silent drift.

appId.machineOverlapAcknowledged: the namespace is deliberately the developer's own name, which is also this machine's username — a chosen personal namespace, not a leaked local value
appId.note: Frozen 2026-07-25 (James). Personal namespace — the convention for an individually-enrolled Apple Developer account, and collision-free without owning a product domain. NOT the same thing as contracts' APP_ID ('vibefield'), which is the truffle mesh app id and data-root slug; see windowsAppUserModelId.

productName.note: Already load-bearing at runtime: app.setName('VibeField') in electron-shell's composition root, and the distribution spec §7.5 builder config.

executableName.note: Frozen 2026-07-25. Matches productName and electron-builder's own default, so Windows shortcuts, the Linux .desktop StartupWMClass and the macOS binary name all agree without a rename (distribution spec §6.3).

macTeamId.note: Frozen 2026-07-25 (James). Apple Developer Team ID — public information: it ships inside every signed app and appears in the Developer ID certificate's OU. The signing CERTIFICATE and its private key are a different matter entirely and live only in the login keychain locally and a protected CI environment (spec §9.4); the checker refuses anything credential-shaped in this file.

windowsPublisher.note: ROUTE DECIDED 2026-07-25: Azure Trusted Signing (no EV hardware token; the cert is short-lived and minted per signing operation). The VALUE still cannot be chosen, and that is not a delay we can shortcut: with Trusted Signing the certificate subject is the identity Microsoft VERIFIES during account setup — an individual or organisation validation that takes days and produces the exact CN string. Guessing it would guarantee a publisher mismatch in the UAC prompt. Fill this in by copying the subject from the first certificate the Trusted Signing account issues, then bump identityRevision.

windowsAppUserModelId.machineOverlapAcknowledged: identical to appId by requirement; the same personal-namespace reasoning applies
windowsAppUserModelId.note: Frozen 2026-07-25, deliberately IDENTICAL to appId: §5.6 requires the AUMID and the installer's application id to agree or taskbar pinning, shortcuts, notifications and updates disagree with each other. ACTION OUTSTANDING: electron-shell still calls app.setAppUserModelId(APP_ID) with contracts' mesh slug 'vibefield' — now that Windows is a GA target this is a real defect, and the runtime must switch to this value before the first Windows package.

trayGuid.note: Minted 2026-07-25 once Windows became a GA target. Preserves the user's chosen notification-area slot across updates. CAUTION (§5.6): Windows keys the reserved slot to the SIGNED binary, so this GUID must not be used by an unsigned build — doing so burns it and the slot is lost for the signed one. It is therefore applied only from the first Authenticode-signed Windows package, not from a local --dir build.

updateChannel.note: First public channel. Stable clients never consume beta metadata (distribution spec §11.4); promotion to 'stable' is an identity event, hence the revision bump.

updateOrigin.machineOverlapAcknowledged: the GitHub account jamesyong-42 is the developer's own; the overlap with the local username is the account name, not a leaked local value
updateOrigin.note: Frozen 2026-07-25 (James): VibeField is open source and both downloads and updates are served from public GitHub Releases. electron-updater's github provider reads metadata from here, and because the repo is public no credential ever reaches an end-user machine — which is what §11.4 requires. Release ASSETS are consequently public too: a 437 MB .app is visible to anyone, which is intended for an open beta.
